en: The Philippines is an archipelago made up of 7,641 islands, making it one of the largest archipelagos in the world.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers on the island of Luzon.
The Sierra Madre mountain range is the longest in the Philippines, stretching approximately 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest oceanic trench in the country, plunging to a maximum depth of 10,540 meters at the Galathea Depth.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is the most active volcano in the Philippines, having erupted over 50 times in the last 400 years.
The island of Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, covering a land area of about 109,965 square kilometers.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River is one of the longest navigable underground rivers in the world, stretching for 8.2 kilometers before reaching the sea.
The Chocolate Hills formation in Bohol consists of at least 1,260 symmetrical limestone mounds spread over an area of 50 square kilometers.
The island of Mindanao is the second-largest island in the Philippines, covering a land area of approximately 97,530 square kilometers.
Found in Bohol, the Philippine Tarsier is one of the world's smallest primates, measuring only 85 to 160 millimeters in total height.
